html:
The Primary Chronicle, or Tale of Bygone Years, is the main history of Kievan Rus', compiled in Kyiv in the 1110s. It covers the years from about 850 to 1110, and much of what we know of the early East Slavs comes from it alone.

Tradition named the monk Nestor of the Kyiv Monastery of the Caves as its author. Scholars now see it as the work of several monks, who reworked older notes, Byzantine chronicles, treaty texts and oral tales, with a final edition around 1116 to 1118.

It describes the East Slavic tribes, such as the Polans and the Krivichs, and their Finnic neighbours, the Chud and the Ves. Its best known stories include:

  • 862: the tribes of the north invite the Varangian Rurik and his brothers to rule them.
  • 882: Oleg takes Kyiv and makes it his capital.
  • 907 and 911: Oleg's campaign against Constantinople and the trade treaty with the Greeks, whose text is copied in.
  • 986 to 988: Vladimir tests the faiths and takes baptism from Byzantium.

Its story of the Varangian founding is much argued over, but it remains the base text for the early history of places such as Kyiv, Novgorod and Polotsk.
